title: Juniper and the Ledger Again
premise: When a parishioner's diary surfaces in the cathedral crypt—still being written two years after her disappearance—archivist Rosalind Montrose realizes the missing woman never left the town at all, and that someone has been maintaining her absence ever since. Following entries that double as coded ledger lines, Rosalind uncovers a scheme of tithes skimmed and secrets laundered through the cathedral's own accounts, kept by people she loves. The trail ends at the tideline, where the tide finally gives up what it took: the woman herself, alive, hiding as the ledger's last keeper. Rosalind must choose between handing her to the law and letting the truth stand without a body to answer for it.
about_author: Sebastian Eastwick is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent a decade cataloguing documents no one was meant to read again. They write mysteries about paper trails and the people who bury them.

chapters.title: The Entry After the End
chapters.summary: POV: Rosalind Montrose. While re-cataloguing the locked crypt after a flood warning, Rosalind finds Edith Vane's diary—its final dated entry written fourteen months after Edith vanished from the tidal flats. The handwriting is unmistakably hers. Rosalind, who prides himself on closable cases, feels the floor of his certainty give way. Emotional beat: quiet dread dressed as professional curiosity.

chapters.title: Tithes Written Twice
chapters.summary: POV: Rosalind. The diary's later entries mirror columns from the cathedral's historic ledgers—figures offset by one line, dates shifted by tides. Rosalind realizes Edith encoded the church's hidden accounts into her own disappearance. When he questions the verger, an old friend, the man's answers are too smooth, and someone searches Rosalind's office overnight. Emotional beat: loyalty curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: POV: Rosalind. Decoding the final ledger sequence, Rosalind traces payments to a decommissioned lighthouse cottage and confronts the verger at the tideline. The truth breaks open: Edith discovered the embezzlement, faked her death with the conspirators' help, then turned informant on them all—and the diary was her insurance, planted where only an archivist would look. Emotional beat: betrayal and revelation colliding at the water's edge.

chapters.title: A Ledger Balanced
chapters.summary: POV: Rosalind. With the tide giving up the lighthouse boat and the conspirators exposed, Rosalind faces his choice: hand Edith to the police or let the ledger speak while she vanishes properly this time. He gives the authorities the accounts but keeps her final page back—a debt paid to belonging over justice. The crypt is relocked, lighter than before. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace, a case closed on his own terms.
